page: Microsoft Azure D11_v2 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dv2 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 2 dedicated physical cores providing 2 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. It is equipped with 14.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 7.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 102 GB, and the instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. No GPU accelerators are included in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the D11_v2 operates in the lower performance tiers. In CPU-intensive tasks, the instance scored 1118.09 on the stress-ng single-core test and 2171.76 on the multi-core test. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 15.16 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.42 GB/sec. Cryptographic and database operations show similar constraints, with a PassMark database operations score of 1108.39 and a Redis SET throughput of 2.22 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D11_v2 offers a legacy hardware profile with a relatively high memory allocation per vCPU, which may benefit workloads requiring more RAM than compute power. However, the overall low benchmark-per-resource performance suggests significant tradeoffs for modern, compute-heavy applications. This server is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, small-scale database operations, or development and testing environments that require moderate memory but do not demand high CPU throughput.
